steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS
steps.instruction: Dilute 10× PBS with deionized water to a final volume of 2 L (200 mL 10× PBS + 1800 mL water) to make 1× PBS; use fresh within 7 days.

steps.title: Prepare 4 % PFA
steps.instruction: Dissolve 4 g paraformaldehyde powder in 90 mL 1× PBS, heat to 60–65 °C, add a few drops of 5 N NaOH until clear, cool, bring to 100 mL with 1× PBS, adjust pH to 7.4; store at –20 °C and thaw 30 min before use.

steps.title: Prepare 2.5 % avertin
steps.instruction: Mix 250 µL 2,2,2‑tribromoethanol with 9.75 mL 1× PBS to a total of 10 mL; store at 4 °C up to 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 M glycine
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.75 g glycine powder in 10 mL 1× PBS in a 15 mL conical tube; store at 4 °C up to 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare 30 % sucrose
steps.instruction: Dissolve 15 g sucrose in 50 mL 1× PBS; store at 4 °C up to 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare blocking buffer
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL conical tube add 9.5 mL 1× PBS, 500 µL horse serum (5 % final), and 0.2 g BSA (2 % final); shake until clear.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Set up a 40 × 50 cm lab mat, restrain mouse, inject 0.5 mL 2.5 % avertin intraperitoneally (≈0.2 mL per 10 g body weight), wait 5 min, confirm lack of tail response; alternatively use isoflurane.

steps.title: Perfuse mouse with PBS
steps.instruction: Pin mouse ventral side up, make midline skin incision from lower abdomen to chest, cut muscle to expose ribcage, open chest, lift heart, cut 0.5–1.5 mm incision in right atrium, insert perfusion needle into left ventricle, perfuse 1× PBS at 10–15 mL/min until effluent runs clear.

steps.title: Dissect hindlimb muscles
steps.instruction: Remove abdominal organs, lift hindlimb skin with fine tweezers, cut fascia with iris scissors, cut knees, incise Achilles tendon at ankle, pull tendon toward knee with super‑fine tweezers, cut tendon at knee to free muscle, remove soleus, lift and cut fascia from gastrocnemius; isolate gastrocnemius (or soleus/TA as alternatives).

steps.title: Fix muscle tissue
steps.instruction: Place gastrocnemius in 4 % PFA (15 mL conical tube) and shake on orbital shaker for 2 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash fixed tissue
steps.instruction: Wash three times with ~10 mL 1× PBS per wash, 10 min each at room temperature on orbital shaker.

steps.title: Cryoprotect in sucrose
steps.instruction: Incubate muscle in 10 mL 30 % sucrose at 4 °C overnight with rotation.

steps.title: Embed in O.C.T.
steps.instruction: Make a cube mold from aluminum foil, fill to 70 % with O.C.T., position muscle longitudinally in center, mark intended cutting plane, freeze by immersing mold (not O.C.T.) in liquid nitrogen (or dry ice) until solid, then store at –80 °C or proceed to cryostat.

steps.title: Cryosection tissue
steps.instruction: Set cryostat to –20 °C, install fresh blade and anti‑roll plate, remove foil, mount O.C.T. block with muscle longitudinally, trim block face to 50 µm, collect 30 µm sections, place each on pre‑labeled slide (≥3 sections per slide), keep slides at room temperature; wrap remaining tissue in foil and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Remove O.C.T. and quench autofluorescence
steps.instruction: Wash slide 3 × 250 mL 1× PBS, 10 min each on orbital shaker at 60 rpm; apply 200 µL 0.1 M glycine, incubate 40 min at room temperature (no shaking); discard glycine, wash 3 × 250 mL 1× PBS, 10 min each at 60 rpm.

steps.title: Block nonspecific binding
steps.instruction: Apply 200 µL blocking buffer to each section, incubate 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate primary antibodies (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare mixture of anti‑synaptophysin and anti‑neurofilament each 1/200 in blocking buffer, apply 200 µL to each section, incubate overnight at 4 °C in a humidified immuno‑pathology staining kit (wet paper towel optional).

steps.title: Wash after primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Wash slide 3 × 250 mL 1× PBS, 10 min each at 60 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Label NMJs and secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Apply 200 µL Alexa‑594‑conjugated α‑bungarotoxin diluted 1/1000 in 1× PBS (add 488‑conjugated donkey anti‑rabbit secondary 1/1000 if secondary needed), incubate 2 h at room temperature in darkness.

steps.title: Wash after α‑bungarotoxin
steps.instruction: Wash slide 3 × 250 mL 1× PBS, 10 min each at 60 rpm, room temperature.

steps.title: Mount with DAPI
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL DAPI fluoromount‑G to each section, lower coverslip slowly to avoid bubbles, seal edges with nail polish, air‑dry in laminar flow cabinet for 20 min.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Turn on confocal microscope and computer, open Zen software, activate laser, mount slide, locate NMJ with 20×/0.8 objective, switch to acquisition mode, set parameters: α‑BTX detection 566–759 nm, DAPI detection 405–481 nm, scaling X/Y 0.277 µm, Z 0.700 µm, lasers 100 % (α‑BTX) and 10 % (DAPI), gain 550 (α‑BTX) and 520 (DAPI), Z‑stack interval 0.7 µm, single‑direction stack; start experiment, capture 3‑D stack, export as TIFF.

description: Validation of protocol Two published papers can validate the measurements of NMJs: Our previously published paper, “Muscle-restricted nuclear receptor interaction protein knockout causes motor neuron degeneration through down-regulation of myogenin at the neuromuscular junction” [4], provides a representative image and quantification of NMJ area in gastrocnemius muscle in Figure 3. The methods for quantifying the NMJ area and calculating the percentage of innervated endplates are demonstrated in Figure 6 of Wong and Martin's 2010 publication, “Skeletal muscle-restricted expression of human SOD1 causes motor neuron degeneration in transgenic mice” [9].
